pr_title: fix(compiler): handle ambient types in input transform function
pr_body:
Fixes that the compiler was throwing an error if an ambient type is used inside of an input `transform` function. The problem was that the reference emitter was trying to write a reference to the ambient type's source file which isn't necessary.

Fixes #51424.
pr_comments: @JoostK I got some time to revisit this PR. I've pushed the changes from https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/51474#discussion_r1304868998 in the `fixup` commit although I'm not exactly sure if this is what you meant.
@JoostK I've addressed 2/3 latest comments and responded on the other one.
Addressed the last comment. The changes are in the final `fixup` commit.
This PR was merged into the repository by commit b98d8f79ed4979fb91661dbdfb6266a917b41474.

issue_context.title: Directive compile broken when using @Input transform
comments: I should add that this is a pretty severe bug - the error messages and side-effects are completely misleading. While there's a workaround (don't use transforms), diagnosing that problem took quite a while - it definitely led to some loss of hair. The only reason this isn't a bigger deal is that @Input transforms probably aren't widely used in the wild, given their newness.

It looks like the actual error is this: 

```
  NG3004: Unable to import type HTMLElement.
  The symbol is not exported from /node_modules/typescript/lib/lib.dom.d.ts.

4           export declare function coerceElement(elementOrRef: HTMLElement | ElementRef<HTMLElement>): HTMLElement;
                                                          ~~~~~~~~~~~

  node_modules/typescript/lib/lib.dom.d.ts:10102:13
    10102 declare var HTMLElement: {
                      ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    10103     prototype: HTMLElement;
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    10104     new(): HTMLElement;
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    10105 };
          ~
    The type is declared here.
```

It's unclear why only the error after it gets logged though, I suspect it might be a CLI issue.

Thanks for the investigation @crisbeto . I don't see that error, and the `coerceElement()` function works fine if I use it elsewhere. I added use of the `coerceElement` fn in the property setter for the comparable directive (MirrorHeightDirective - no Input transform) that works fine - `git pull` for that change.

Here's the build output I see:

```

$ ng build util && ng build ui-components

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

libs/ui-components/sticky/src/Sticky.component.ts:10:5 - error NG2012: Component imports must be standalone components, directives, pipes, or must be NgModules.

10     MirrorWidthDirective
       ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

error Command failed with exit code 1.
info Visit https://yarnpkg.com/en/docs/cli/run for documentation about this command.
```

Further, the MirrorWidthDirective class/file is compiled into the output .mjs file, it's just missing the normal annotations in the build output as described above. If there was a compile error referencing the lib function, I would expect that the class wouldn't be in the build output file.

There are a few things going on:
1. Angular won't compile a class if it contains errors. That's why it was failing later on saying that `imports` must contain directives or pipes.
2. The class compilation fails, because the compiler needs to be able to reference the type of the first parameter in the `transform` function. It fails here, because `HTMLElement` is an ambient type and our code wasn't accounting for such types. I've sent out #51474 to fix it.
3. It's unclear why the error for `HTMLElement` wasn't being logged, but my best guess is that the CLI is suppressing it since I could see the error when I moved your use case into the compiler's unit tests.

Thank you for the explanation and fix @crisbeto. I'm thinking there are more bugs than just the input transform function not handling ambient types. But I don't know enough about them to create the bug reports + repro cases:

* Why does the compiler write `class MirrorWidthDirective` to `dist\ui-components\fesm2022\ui-components-mirror-size.mjs` in a broken state? It seems like it should not be in the output file if compiling the class failed.
* Why is the error not being reported?

I'm concerned that just fixing the transform error will leave these as latent problems that will bite users later.

1. `MirrorWidthDirective` is being written by TypeScript. Angular doesn't write its metadata if there are errors. We probably don't want to go and omit the class ourselves because it might be referenced elsewhere.
2. I'm not sure why the error isn't being reported, because I am seeing it in unit test. My guess is that the CLI's error logging only shows the bottom error in the stack.
Thank you for the reply @crisbeto. Both of those seem like problems. Should there at least be a bug for #2?
@CSchulz  - can you report the compile error you're getting? Is it the same as I reported in this issue, or is it less misleading?

review_comments: Context here: in #43511 we added some assertions around not allowing classes defined inside namespaces. I added this flag so we only allow ambient references in specific places (input transforms in this case).
I can't think of a reason why we wouldn't want this behavior if `AllowTypeImports` is used; can the new condition just use the `AllowTypeImports` flag instead of introducing a new mode?
It looks like using `AllowTypeImports` also allows the behavior we were guarding against in #43511.
That is somewhat unexpected to me 🤔
Can the tests in `type_parameter_emitter_spec.ts` be expanded with coverage for ambient types?
